summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes the only SSRF guard on outbound webhook delivery and lets the runner POST arbitrary event payloads to any customer-supplied URL.

## Analysis

`deliver()` previously resolved the URL hostname and rejected anything outside `ALLOWED_HOSTS`. That check is gone. With a controllable `url`, an attacker (or a misconfigured tenant) can point delivery at:

- Cloud metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`, etc.)
- localhost / link-local / RFC1918 services reachable from the runner
- Non-HTTP schemes that `urllib.request` will still open

The PR description frames this as an enterprise feature, but opening the host set requires an explicit allowlist, HTTPS-only policy, private-IP block, or egress proxy — not deletion of the gate.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The patch removes ALLOWED_HOSTS and the urlsplit hostname check from deliver(), so urlopen now POSTs to any caller-supplied URL with no host restriction—an SSRF regression matching the claim.
